A RET is a transmembrane (TM) tyrosine kinase receptor with multiple cadherin-like domains (CLD), a juxtamembrane cysteine-rich domain (CRD), and a split intracellular kinase (TrK). RET ligands include GDNF, artemin, persephin, and neurturin, which bind the RET co-receptors GFRα 1–4. B Ligand-dependent activation results from dimerization, autophosphorylation, and activation of RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK and PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling. C Ligand-independent activation results from RET proto-oncogene variants that cause dimerization, most often in the extracellular CRD but also in the transmembrane or intracellular domains, or as a monomer due to the presence of a RET proto-oncogene variant in the intracellular tyrosine kinase domain. GFLs, glial cell line–derived neurotrophic factor family ligands; GIP, glycosylphosphatidylinositol; MEN2A, multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A; FMTC, familial medullary thyroid carcinoma.
